title: TrustLens Indicator Observation
description: Phase 2 WP2 STEP 5. The TYPED BOUNDARY between the extraction layer and the deterministic rule engine. An indicator observation asserts that a named registry/library indicator was (or was not) observed in an input, with what confidence, backed by which normalized observations and spans. It is the object the rule engine consumes: the current rule_runner takes the SET { indicator_id : matched == OBSERVED } as its signal set, so this contract is a strict, backward-compatible superset of today's hand-declared expected_indicators. An extractor emits indicator observations; it MUST NOT declare a scam, risk, severity or final verdict — that is the rule/detection layer's job (FR/CONF-001). The schema forbids a verdict structurally (additionalProperties:false with no such field); validate_extraction.py additionally rejects any forbidden key by name as defence in depth.

indicator_id.description: Must resolve to a POSITIVE indicator in indicator-registry-v0.json or a NEGATIVE indicator in negative-indicator-library-v1.json. A DEPRECATED indicator may not be emitted (checked by the linter, matching validate_rules.py L1b).

indicator_version.description: Version of the indicator definition this observation was produced against (library indicators carry a version; the positive registry is versioned as a whole). Lets a finding record exactly which indicator semantics ran (KB-001 §7).

polarity.description: Must equal the polarity the indicator carries in the registry/library. A POSITIVE indicator observation is a scam-supporting signal; a NEGATIVE one is suppressive. The linter fails a mismatch.

matched.description: STEP 12. Whether the indicator fired. Only OBSERVED enters the rule engine's signal set. NOT_OBSERVED records an affirmative absence (useful for negative context and for explanation). AMBIGUOUS/UNKNOWN keep uncertainty as uncertainty rather than collapsing to benign.

confidence.description: STEP 10. EXTRACTION confidence that this indicator is present — 'how sure are we that this text requests an OTP'. NOT rule confidence and NOT a fraud probability. The rule engine currently uses presence (OBSERVED), not this number.

observation_refs.description: observation_ids (observation.schema.json) that support this indicator. The bridge that makes an indicator explainable: an indicator with no supporting observation is unexplainable and SHOULD NOT be emitted (the linter warns).

supporting_spans.description: Character spans in the source text evidencing the indicator, so the explanation chain reaches the exact words (FR-046/047).

input_id.description: The envelope this indicator observation was derived from.

extraction_method.description: How this indicator was produced. COMPOSED = derived from multiple observations by a deterministic composition rule (e.g. RECEIVE_FRAMING from a payment_direction fact). The concrete method mix is a later-phase decision; WP2 reserves the vocabulary.

family_ref.description: The indicator-families-v1.json family this indicator belongs to. Optional on an instance (derivable from the family map) but useful for grouped explanation.

review_required.description: Whether this observation should be routed to human review before being trusted (e.g. AMBIGUOUS payment direction, low-confidence LLM extraction). Advisory to the pipeline; never itself a finding.

provenance.description: STEP 11. Extractor identity/type/version behind this indicator observation.

score.description: Advisory extraction score. Never a fraud probability (CONF-001).
